paper_metadata.title: Variational quantum simulations of stochastic differential equations

experiments.description: Variational quantum simulation of a discretized stochastic differential equation using a trinomial tree model, validated on geometric Brownian motion with a 4-qubit ansatz of depth k=2 and k=3.

algorithm.variant: Variational quantum simulation of trinomial-tree discretized SDE probability distributions
algorithm.ansatz: Real-amplitude hardware-efficient ansatz with CNOT and RY gates

problem_formulation.objective_function: Simulate the time evolution of the probability distribution P(X(t)=x_i) governed by the linear differential equation derived from the trinomial tree approximation of the SDE.

problem_instance.description: Geometric Brownian motion SDE with drift mu(X(t),t)=rX(t) and diffusion sigma(X(t),t)=sigma X(t), simulated on a discretized lattice.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic stochastic process; parameters r=0.1, sigma=0.2, delta_x=1, time interval t in [0,4].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Trinomial tree discretization of the SDE; probability distribution directly embedded in amplitudes of an unnormalized quantum state.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Classical noiseless simulation of the quantum circuit using numpy and jax; comparison against analytical solution of the SDE/Fokker-Planck equation and Runge-Kutta solution of the linear differential equation.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Runge-Kutta method; analytical Fokker-Planck solution for comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize SDE into trinomial tree; set n=4 qubits and depth-k ansatz with k=2.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute mean and variance from the resulting probability distribution; compare to analytical and Runge-Kutta results.

classical_baselines.method_name: analytical solution of the sde/fokker-planck equation

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical simulation / quantum linear solver approaches
speedup_claims.conditions: for SDEs whose drift and diffusion can be expressed with small-degree polynomial expansions; VQS with O(poly(n)) resources when m_max is small
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical runtime speedup is reported; the paper argues resource advantages over QLSA and classical Monte Carlo in principle.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(Poly(n)) for VQS simulation when m_max is small; O(n m_max) distinct unitaries per time step in L(t) decomposition
